title: Frightened by another’s trouble
odia:
ବିରି ମାଡ଼ ଶୁଣି କୋଳଥ ଚୋପା
ହରଡ଼ କହୁଛି ରଖଲୋ ବାପା ॥
literal_meaning: Hearing the black gram being beaten, horse-gram husk; the pigeon pea says, “Save me, father.”
explanation: The source explains the fear that spreads when someone sees another in trouble. The pulses speak as if the next blow might reach them too.
meaning_odia: ଅନ୍ୟ ଜଣଙ୍କ ଉପରେ ବିପଦ ପଡ଼ିବା ଦେଖି ନିଜେ ଭୟ ପାଇବାର କଥା ଏହା। ନିଜ ପାଳି ଆସିଯିବ କି ବୋଲି ଆଶଙ୍କା ଜାଗେ।
usage_example: One shop is penalised for unsafe wiring, and neighbouring owners anxiously inspect their own shops. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: The first clause is elliptical in the captured wording. It is preserved without supplying a missing verb; the source gloss supports the shared-fear reading.
